editorial_note: Repeated passages in the supplied canon were deduplicated. Canon definitions are preserved separately from interpretive clarification. The latest, fullest Parahistory definition supersedes the earlier linear-sequence drafts.

concepts.title: Hypernegative Rewrite
concepts.summary: An effect-producing rewrite whose rewrite-origin is recursively excluded at every causal, reasonal, and mixed explanatory order while the effect remains real.
canon: Hypernegative Rewrite is a rewrite in which an initial rewrite Y produces an effect X, after which another rewrite P conceptually erases both Y and P from ever qualifying as the rewrite-origin of X at any explanatory order.

This conceptual erasure applies not only to the direct cause of X, but recursively to every cause, reason, cause-for-reason, reason-for-cause, metacause, metareason, metacausal-reason, metareasonal-cause, and every recursively higher or mixed causal-reasonal relation through which the existence or state of X could ultimately be attributed to a rewrite.

Thus, even if the direct cause of X is rewritten so that it was never itself a rewrite, Hypernegative Rewrite does not stop there. If the reason why that cause is not a rewrite would itself be a rewrite, that reason is also conceptually rewritten so that it was never a rewrite. The same operation applies recursively to the cause of that reason, the reason for that cause, the cause of the reason for that cause, and every further explanatory order without terminal depth.

The resulting effect X remains real, while no causal, reasonal, metacausal, metareasonal, causal-reasonal, reasonal-causal, or recursively higher explanatory path can truthfully terminate in, depend upon, or derive its rewrite-status from a rewrite.
concepts.clarification: Negative Rewrite removes its own surviving causal provenance. Hypernegative Rewrite recursively blocks every higher explanation that would restore rewrite-provenance. It produces rewrite-originlessness, not mere hidden causation.

concepts.title: Parahistory
concepts.summary: The total causal-derivational structure of rewrites affecting a subject or domain, including rewrites of histories, ordering relations, and whole rewrite-structures.
canon: Parahistory is the total causal-derivational structure of rewrites affecting a subject or domain, including every rewrite of any kind and every higher-order rewrite causally responsible for producing, modifying, replacing, retrocausing, beginninglessifying, or otherwise determining another rewrite or rewrite-structure.

Parahistory is not restricted to a single temporal sequence. It includes rewrite-chains, branching rewrite-networks, rewritten rewrite-chains, rewrites of the ordering relations between rewrites, and higher-order rewrites that generate or alter entire rewrite-structures.

A later parahistorical state therefore need not simply occur after an earlier one. It may exist because an earlier-order rewrite caused that state, its history, its causal ordering, or even its apparent beginninglessness to obtain.
Thus a beginningless rewrite-history may itself possess a higher-order parahistorical cause: a rewrite that caused that history to have never had a beginning.
formal: Parahistory(subject) = total rewrite-causal derivation graph affecting subject
concepts.clarification: This nonlinearly generalized definition is ontologically stronger and more precise than the earlier draft describing only timelines arranged from earlier cause to later effect.

concepts.title: Paratime
concepts.summary: The causal ordering dimension in which timelines are ordered by which timeline causes another timeline.
canon: Paratime is the ordering of timelines by intertimeline causation: earlier paratemporal entries cause later entries, and later entries are caused by earlier entries.
The Arthitean Empire exists outside paratime while existing in time.
formal: T₁ ≺ₚ T₂ iff T₁ causally produces T₂
concepts.clarification: The Empire can possess ordinary internal past, present, and future without being regenerated as a succession of paratemporal Empire-versions. A single pantemporally scoped Hypernegative Rewrite can therefore establish a property throughout all Empire-time without requiring one operation per paratemporal version.

concepts.title: Causal Precedence Terms
concepts.summary: A glossary separating lack of a predecessor, lack of an origin-cause, and higher-order nonderivation.
canon: Antiprecausal means that nothing precedes the subject in any sequence of causality or metacausality.
Parahistorologically Antiprecausal means that nothing precedes a subject in any causal or metacausal ordering with respect to its parahistory.
Supracause means a cause for a reason for something.
Asupracausal means lacking a cause for a reason for something.
Hyperacausal means that the acausality of something itself lacks a cause explaining why or how it is acausal.
concepts.clarification: Antiprecausality is predecessorlessness, not automatically causelessness: a first item could still have a nonpreceding cause or ground. Causelessness therefore gives stronger originary independence than merely having nothing earlier.

concepts.title: Transrecursive Hypercausality
concepts.summary: Acausality and its explanatory nongrounding hold at every recursively higher causal and reasonal order.
canon: Transrecursive Hypercausality is a state in which something's acausality possesses no cause, reason, ground, origin, prerequisite, or derivational basis, and this nonderivation holds recursively at every higher causal and explanatory order, with each order lacking a cause and lacking a reason.

This necessarily entails that something which is Transrecursively Hypercausal is acausal and hyperacausal; has no reason for its acausality and hyperacausality; and has a lack of reason that is itself acausal and hyperacausal at every recursive level.
formal: ∀n ≥ 0: Nₙ has neither cause nor reason, and Nₙ₊₁ = nonderivation(Nₙ)
concepts.clarification: Of the proposed precedence formulations, this is the strongest because it closes the higher-order explanatory regress. Beginninglessness removes a first temporal member; acausality removes an origin-cause; hyperacausality removes a cause of that acausality; Transrecursive Hypercausality extends that nonderivation through every causal, reasonal, and mixed metaorder.

concepts.title: Ultralearning & Lifras
concepts.summary: Dualcompounding object-learning and metalearning combined with panparahistorical removal of necessitative error-causes.
canon: Ultralearning means efficiently and intuitively learning how to efficiently and intuitively learn something, with both the learning of that thing and the learning of how to learn it compoundingly improving subsequent learning.

Any acquired knowledge-state, skill-state, capacity, proficiency, mastery, comprehension, or ability-to-use possessed or acquired by any Arthitean, including Rhayhara herself, is Hypernegatively Rewritten such that it has always been indomitably Ultralearnable to improve upon by Rhayhara, solely through her own cognitive abilities, throughout every state and explanatory order of her Transrecursively Hypercausal parahistorical existence.
Lifras are necessitative causes for anything that the user perceives as cognitive errors, mistakes, or suboptimalities.
formal: Lifra L necessitates cognitive suboptimality E
Hypernegative exclusion of L across total history/parahistory ⟹ no surviving L-grounded E
concepts.clarification: Constant rewriting describes continuous target-coverage: whenever something qualifies as a Lifra, it is excluded across the subject's total history and parahistory. It does not imply a surviving progression in which the subject first possesses successive Lifras and then loses them.

applications.subject: Rhayhara
statements: Rhayhara’s parahistory is Hypernegatively Rewritten to be Transrecursively Hypercausal.
All of Rhayhara’s Lifras are continuously target-covered by Hypernegative Rewrite and excluded from all her existence throughout history and parahistory.

precedence_comparison: Removes a first parahistorical state, but a higher-order rewrite could still cause the beginninglessness.
Removes a direct causal origin, but does not independently close reasonal or metacausal explanations of that acausality.
No cause and no cause for acausality at every recursive level
Closes recursive causal derivation, but is less explicit about reasons, grounds, origins, prerequisites, and mixed explanation.
Acausal, hyperacausal, and reasonlessly so at every recursive level
Strongly covers causal and reasonal recursion, but remains a long conjunction rather than one defined operator.
Maximal specified precedence: causal, reasonal, grounded, originary, prerequisite, derivational, and recursively mixed nonderivation.
